Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

get verb

obtain, come by

also obtain, acquire, get hold of, come by, get back, now get this

classical

Cic. Amic. 55: amīcōs nōn parāre
Cic. Att. 12.19.1: trāns Tiberim hortōs (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 320

parō, parāre, parāvī, parātum

verb, first conjugation

get, acquire (often by buying)

Of getting what one sets out to have: friends, a garden, provisions; with money, “buy” (Lewis & Short). Its first sense is “prepare”.

Other words

  • nancīscor, nancīscī, nactus (nānctus) sum — get, come upon, obtain

    verb, third conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Traupman 320; Cic. Fam. 3.7.1: cum plūs ōtī nactus erō

    Of what comes one’s way rather than what one works for (Lewis & Short): time, a chance, someone to carry a letter.

  • adipīscor, adipīscī, adeptus sum — obtain, reach (by effort)

    verb, third conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Sen. 4: quam ut adipīscantur omnēs optant

    Of what is reached with effort: old age, honours, wisdom.

  • impetrō, impetrāre, impetrāvī, impetrātum — get (by asking), have a request granted

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Phaedr. 1.19.5: facile impetrāvit; Cic. Fam. 13.36.1 (Lewis & Short)

    What one gets by asking: impetrāvī, “I got what I asked for”.

  • accipiō, accipere, accēpī, acceptum — get, receive

    verb, third conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 320

Examples

  • plūribus verbīs ad tē scrībam, cum plūs ōtī nactus erō

    I’ll write to you at more length when I get more free timeCic. Fam. 3.7.1

  • canis parturiēns cum rogāsset alteram ut fētum in ejus tuguriō dēpōneret, facile impetrāvit

    a dog about to have puppies asked another to let her lay her litter in her kennel, and easily got her wayPhaedr. 1.19.3–5

  • amīcōs nōn parāre, optimam et pulcherrimam vītae, ut ita dīcam, supellectilem

    … and not to get friends, the best and finest furniture of life, so to speakCic. Amic. 55

  • repetere, recipere

    to get backTraupman 320

  • prōmere

    to get out, bring outTraupman 320

  • Nōn queō ōrāre ut loquātur.

    I can’t get him to talk.Traupman 320

  • Nunc cognōsce rem.

    Now get this.Traupman 320

See also receive, get, buy, become, reach.
